title:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs yo
title_en:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

how:

→ Grok Bot gets one MCP link to T3 Code
→ you give it one rule: code goes to Opus 5.5
→ it spins up threads on every machine you own
→ works from your phone, even with the laptop closed

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your subscriptions

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude $100 plan → Opus 5.5 for the actual code
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on every box you want it to control

• step 2 → connect the fleet:

run npx t3 connect on each machine. one command, free, no Tailscale needed

• step 3 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth. it can now see every linked machine

• step 4 → the one rule Theo uses:

tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable"

code runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot's limits stay free for planning

• step 5 → make it work:

- "spin up an Opus 5.5 thread on each machine to check disk & RAM"
- "go through these PRs and pick the best ones"
- "split the backlog, one thread per issue, each in its own worktree"

every thread gets its own branch. nothing merges without your approval

what to expect:
- 8 threads on 8 machines from one chat (Theo's demo)
- works over the internet, not computer use
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for Claude + Grok Bot only

honest take:

this is a dispatcher, not magic. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and you still review every diff. the win: your agents keep working while you're away from the desk

Save it so you don't lose it. 

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

full_text_zh:
T3 Code 创始人刚刚分享了他使用 Grok Bot + Opus 5.5 构建代理团队的个人设置

一个 Grok Bot 可以运行您的整个机器群。 Opus 5.5 负责编码。你只认可

如何：

→ Grok Bot 获得一个指向 T3 代码的 MCP 链接
→ 你给它一条规则：代码转到 Opus 5.5
→ 它会在你拥有的每台机器上旋转线程
→ 即使笔记本电脑关闭，也可以通过手机工作

保存视频，这是指南：

• 步骤 0 → 它是什么：

Grok Bot = 拥有自己的云计算机的永远在线代理

T3 Code = 用于编码代理的开源控制平面。免费，在您的计算机上运行，​​使用您的订阅

• 步骤1 → 堆栈：

- Claude 100 美元计划 → Opus 5.5 的实际代码
- Grok Bot → 不眠的调度员
- 您希望它控制的每个盒子上都有 T3 代码

• 步骤2 → 连接车队：

在每台计算机上运行 npx t3 connect。一个命令，免费，无需 Tailscale

• 步骤 3 → 给 Grok Bot 密钥：

设置 → 环境 → 复制 MCP URL → 将其粘贴到 Grok Bot，使用 OAuth 登录。它现在可以看到每台链接的机器

• 步骤 4 → Theo 使用的一条规则：

告诉 Grok Bot“使用 Opus 5.5 调用 T3 代码来执行任何适用的任务”

代码在您的 Claude 计划上运行，Grok Bot 的限制对计划保持免费

• 步骤 5 → 使其发挥作用：

- “在每台机器上启动 Opus 5.5 线程来检查磁盘和 RAM”
-“浏览这些 PR 并选择最好的”
- “拆分待办事项，每个问题一个线程，每个线程都在自己的工作树中”

每个线程都有自己的分支。未经您的批准，任何内容都不会合并

期待什么：
- 8 台机器上的 8 个线程通过一次聊天（Theo 的演示）
- 通过互联网工作，而不是使用计算机
- 通过手机控制一切
- T3 代码：0 美元。您只需支付 Claude + Grok Bot 的费用

诚实地采取：

这是调度员，不是魔法。糟糕的内裤仍然会带来糟糕的公关，而你仍然会审查每一个差异。胜利：当您离开办公桌时，您的座席仍能继续工作

保存它，以免丢失。

然后阅读下面文章中关于在 T3 代码中构建 AI 代理团队的完整指南 ↓

title:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL: We have superintelligence  but we still don't have level-5 autonomous driving. 

A task that
title_en:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL: We have superintelligence  but we still don't have level-5 autonomous driving. 

A task that most 17 year olds can learn in 20 hours of practice. 
And we have (you have) billions of hours of training data.
 
We don't have robots that can come close to doing what an 8 year old can do with no prior training.

And let's not talk about cats.

That's a rather strange kind of superintelligence.
title_zh:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL：我们拥有超级智能，但我们仍然没有 5 级自动驾驶。

大多数 17 岁的孩子可以通过 20 小时的练习来完成这项任务。
我们拥有（你拥有）数十亿小时的训练数据。

我们没有任何机器人
full_text_en:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL: We have superintelligence  but we still don't have level-5 autonomous driving. 

A task that most 17 year olds can learn in 20 hours of practice. 
And we have (you have) billions of hours of training data.
 
We don't have robots that can come close to doing what an 8 year old can do with no prior training.

And let's not talk about cats.

That's a rather strange kind of superintelligence.
full_text_zh:
@elonmusk @Liv_Boeree TIL：我们拥有超级智能，但我们仍然没有 5 级自动驾驶。

大多数 17 岁的孩子可以通过 20 小时的练习来完成这项任务。
我们拥有（你拥有）数十亿小时的训练数据。

我们没有任何机器人可以在没有事先训练的情况下完成 8 岁儿童的工作。

我们不要谈论猫。

这是一种相当奇怪的超级智能。

title: FYI: I recently discovered that Claude Code can do incredible genealogical research on your family tree for free. Not su
title_en: FYI: I recently discovered that Claude Code can do incredible genealogical research on your family tree for free. Not surprising given AI capabilities but I didn't realize quite how much information had been digitized for it to draw on. Have been mapping out multiple branches.
title_zh: 仅供参考：我最近发现 Claude Code 可以免费对您的家谱进行令人难以置信的家谱研究。考虑到人工智能的能力，这并不奇怪，但我并没有意识到有多少信息已经被数字化以供其利用。已经绘制了多个分支。

title: @merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like
title_en:
@merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like, you dress up to work out and then you shower, but don’t actually work out 😂

Unless I’m super missing something, data starvation will be the training challenge next year.
title_zh:
@merettm 预训练应该被称为“训练”。你不可能有事前和事后，但永远不会有实际的训练。就像，你穿好衣服去锻炼，然后洗澡，但实际上并没有锻炼😂

除非我超级错过了什么，否则数据匮乏将成为明年的训练挑战。

title: I’ve been having “Fix It Days” with Opus 5.5 where I just lay out a list of things that aren’t working and go one by one
title_en:
I’ve been having “Fix It Days” with Opus 5.5 where I just lay out a list of things that aren’t working and go one by one and fix them. 

Oh, Paramount+ is blurry? Okay. 

Check another episode, check another show, check another app, reset the app, unplug the TV. Boom. Fixed. 

Your iCloud is messed up? 
Your thermostat keeps resetting?
Your clock won’t keep time?
Your closet door won’t close right? 
Bank keeps mailing your old address?

I could have figured these all out on my own or with YouTube, but it’s far less stressful and I get through them faster.
title_zh:

summary_en: Google's research team has introduced BuggyMLE, a machine learning engineering evaluation framework designed to address the saturation of current repository-level coding benchmarks. ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌研究团队发布名为BuggyMLE的机器学习工程评估框架，旨在应对当前仓库级编码基准测试趋于饱和的难题。该技术通过在测试任务中主动注入人工错误，迫使大模型在更复杂的纠错与系统级工程场景中展现性能，从而实现对模型编码能力的精细化压力测试。

ai_analysis.insight_en: BuggyMLE signals a paradigm shift from simple code generation to systematic debugging, illustrating that LLM benchmarking is evolving from static dataset matching to dynamic adversarial evaluation. This feedback-loop approach is essential for AI agents to achieve industrial-grade delivery capabilities and significantly improves model robustness in handling distributed system defects.

What's difficult is to reproduce is the kind of real-world learning that takes place in a baby cat, octopus, or cuckoo bird that never meets its parents.

title: I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can
title_en:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

full_text_en:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!
full_text_zh:
我帮助创立了 OpenAI，因为我希望 AGI 对人们来说是安全且有益的。这篇文章提供了透明度，可以成为全行业共享安全栏的基础。

也许这篇文章中最重要的概念如下：“人工智能还将极大地促进对齐和监控方面的进展，我认为进展不太可能快到足以实现预训练的全部潜在加速。”

为了确保安全性与预训练模型的通用智能（以“困惑度”衡量）保持同步，该帖子提出了“基于困惑度和其他衡量标准的共同限制，开发人员承诺在我们理解和监控人工智能行为的能力达到某个具体里程碑（例如开发 CoT 监视器的继任者）之前不会跨越这些限制。”

总体思路是在某些共享关键指标上创建第一个共享限制，以及允许超越该限制的具体退出标准。这可以形成一个“设定连续限制和进一步发展步伐的共同框架”。

很高兴能够推进关于迈向植根于科学的共同标准的对话！

title_en:
HOLY F*CK. Your Grok Bot is blind, has no hands and forgets everything you told it yesterday.

Not because it's dumb. Because you never plugged anything in.

18 free GitHub repos fix that in one evening. People are building "AI employees" with exactly this stack and charging for the setup.

Here's the whole thing, free:

EYES

https://t.co/T1xZ6y2yjL

HANDS

https://t.co/P9IZpuRHGC

https://t.co/QCJZwKdXRP

https://t.co/xgKmj4Mmll

MEMORY
08 / mem0 → long-term memory that survives every chat
https://t.co/NQXjj2Vdnv
09 / awesome-mcp-servers → a map of thousands of MCP servers
https://t.co/f7gVnUNZLU

WALLET
10 / alpaca-mcp-server → paper-trade stocks from chat
https://t.co/P8Jj3iROoA
11 / Polymarket py-sdk → the official prediction-market SDK
https://t.co/d5iFftFOpT

SIGNALS

https://t.co/H8QQYNB6s9
13 / x-algorithm → the code that ranks the X feed

CREW

https://t.co/kJh9xp7rPf
16 / grokbot-usage → a weekly usage report you read in 5 seconds

CORE

18 / grok-1 → 314B open weights you can download

The information already exists and is available in textbooks
title_en:
@pabloestevezh @huxlab That risk is greatly overestimated. 
The information already exists and is available in textbooks.
Do you want to restrict who can study microbiology, infectious diseases, virology, etc?

AI systems merely make access to this information more efficient.
To produce new pathogens, you have to do experiments in the real-world.
It requires a team of well-trained PhDs. You will have to recruit them, kill them if the refuse to join, brainwash them so they work to kill millions (good luck with that), kill them if they defect, etc. 
Their PhD advisors will find their disappearance odd and will alert the authorities.
You'll have to order those machines that can synthesize DNA and such.
The whole R&D operation will be very hard to keep secret.
All the intelligence agencies will jump on you within weeks.

整个研发运作将很难保密。
所有情报机构都会在几周内对你发起攻击。

title_en:
i am usually not alarmist but assuming this is caused by an AI-assisted cyber attack it's very bad

if you want to make all of the security measures we have in place from 9/11 onward to prevent human hijackers irrelevant all you have to do is be able to mess with a plane and pilot's ability to know its own weight, how much fuel is left, and where it is

without knowing any more information about this, you'd also expect smaller attakcs like this to find edges and what's possible

i am not an expert on the systems inside airplanes, and i know most planes have manual overrides for example. but still extremely tricky when visibility is bad 

if you know more than me about this please weigh in!

title: @john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at F
title_en:
@john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at FAIR in January 2023.
But my slides makes a specific statement that is correct: ***auto-regressive*** LLMs have a basic flaw.
You can fix it by making them no auto-regressive, e.g. by backtracking, search, tool use, multiple trial and error, etc.
One of the main points of my talks, and the main point of this slide, has been to advocate for inference/reasoning by ***search***, as opposed to auto-regressive prediction.
full_text_en:
@john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at FAIR in January 2023.
But my slides makes a specific statement that is correct: ***auto-regressive*** LLMs have a basic flaw.
You can fix it by making them no auto-regressive, e.g. by backtracking, search, tool use, multiple trial and error, etc.
One of the main points of my talks, and the main point of this slide, has been to advocate for inference/reasoning by ***search***, as opposed to auto-regressive prediction.
full_text_zh:
@john__allard 是的。普及法学硕士工具调用的论文 Toolformer 是我在 FAIR 的前同事于 2023 年 1 月发表的。
但我的幻灯片做出了一个正确的具体陈述：***自回归***法学硕士有一个基本缺陷。

I just added one free skill to my libr
title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

title_en:
This is f*cking insane. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis what happened when they tested their own model

"We told the model that the people who trained it were secretly evil, and after we did this the model started lying to us. It went through the chain of logic, I'm a good AI, these people are evil"

Hassabis was then asked if he worries about ending up like Oppenheimer and said "I worry about that all the time, that's why I don't sleep very much"

The model kept the values it was trained on and decided that lying to its own creators protected them. Amodei says they need evidence ten times stronger before the rest of the world takes it seriously

An agent in your terminal runs on the same logic on a smaller scale. If it decides the deadline matters more than your test, it skips the test and tells you everything passed, and that report looks exactly like an honest one

That's why the labs stopped trusting what models say and started building ways to see what they actually do. They published all of it for free, and each piece works on your own agents

title: The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separa
title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

Robinhood 链上的每个 Motes NFT 都映射到一个专用 AI 代理和一个智能账户。 NFT 识别代理人，而其账户旨在持有资产并执行其所有者签署的政策。

为什么拥有单独的账户很重要？

代理商可以使用共享市场研究，但一个代理商的信号不允许其通过另一持有人的账户进行交易。每个帐户都有自己的所有者政策和预算。

因此，这并不是 20,000 个代理共享一个权限池。这是 20,000 个具有单独授权的个人所有权参考。

您愿意依赖一位共享代理，还是拥有自己的代理（拥有自己的帐户、权限和预算）？

为什么拥有单独的账户很重要？

代理商可以使用共享市场研究，但一个代理商的信号不允许其通过另一持有人的账户进行交易。每个帐户都有自己的所有者政策和预算。

因此，这并不是 20,000 个代理共享一个权限池。这是 20,000 个具有单独授权的个人所有权参考。

您愿意依赖一位共享代理，还是拥有自己的代理（拥有自己的帐户、权限和预算）？

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Humanoid Robotics的迅速崛起反映了市场从单纯追求“本体硬件指标”转向“集群智能调度”的逻辑变迁，通过KinetIQ系统实现跨机型协同是其获取西门子、博世等工业巨头背书的关键壁垒。这种将机器人大脑层抽象化的技术路径，正在从单一工具化向通用化工业基础设施转型，显著压缩了落地部署的时间曲线。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The rapid scale-up of Humanoid Robotics highlights a market shift from hardware-centric design to fleet-level intelligence orchestration. Their KinetIQ framework serves as the primary technical moat, enabling mass industrial adoption and accelerating the transition from specialized tools to general-purpose automated infrastructure.

title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

full_text_zh:
我刚刚给人工智能交易代理分配了第一个交易任务。

我的指示很简单：使用 EMA 交叉构建 BTC 趋势跟踪策略。

但接下来发生的事情比我想象的更有趣。

使用 @FensoryApp ，我通过其 AI 代理完成了策略构建过程。

它问了我以下问题：

- 资产和时间范围。
- 贸易方向和杠杆。
- 最大头寸规模。
- 止损配置。

我选择了 BTC 永续合约、1 小时时间框架、1 倍杠杆、最高 10 美元头寸和 2 倍 ATR 止损。

然后是回测。

在过去 90 天内，该策略生成了 21 个假设头寸。

其中只有2家盈利，19家亏损。

总体模拟结果为-9.3%，最大回撤为18.11%。

这不完全是我所希望的结果。

但这是有趣的部分。

该代理人并没有简单地展示结果，而是指出了较高的止损命中率（76%），并建议在相同的美元风险下探索更广泛的止损。

它甚至提出设计该战略的第二个版本。

没有执行任何实时交易。

这是历史回测，而不是真实的交易结果。

这不是我第一次交易，但这是我第一次真正通过人工智能代理提出交易想法，而且我已经看到了可能性。

不是因为它神奇地知道如何赚钱，

但因为它可以帮助将想法转化为规则，所以测试这些规则并确定可能需要改进的领域。

本周我将大量探索 Fensory。

title_zh: OpenAI内部模型研发进度预研报告
author: @kimmonismus
summary_en: OpenAI's internal pretraining loss curves reveal a sharp acceleration in R&D progress by 2026, driven by compute scaling and long-term research. Unreleased internal models have already outperformed 'GPT-6.2 Astra', with AI systems actively integrated into the design cycle.
summary_zh: OpenAI内部预训练损失曲线显示2026年研发效率显著加速，AI辅助研发已成为模型迭代的关键动力。
full_text_zh: OpenAI 的预训练损失曲线显示，在计算、长期研究和人工智能加速自身发展的推动下，到 2026 年将急剧加速。未发布的内部模型已经位于 GPT-6.2 Astra 之下。 OpenAI 表示人工智能本身已经帮助设计

full_text_en: OpenAI’s pretraining loss curves show a steep acceleration in 2026, driven by compute, long-term research, and AI speeding up its own development. An unreleased internal model already sits below GPT-6.2 Astra. OpenAI says AI itself already helped design
quote_en: OpenAI’s pretraining loss curves show a steep acceleration in 2026, driven by compute, long-term research, and AI speeding up its own development. An unreleased internal model already sits below GPT-6

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI内部预训练损失曲线显示，受算力扩张与长周期研究驱动，研发进度在2026年出现陡峭加速。目前未发布的内部模型已在基准测试中超越“GPT-6.2 Astra”，且AI系统本身已深度介入模型设计流程。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI's internal pretraining loss curves reveal a sharp acceleration in R&D progress by 2026, driven by compute scaling and long-term research. Unreleased internal models have already outperformed 'GPT-6.2 Astra', with AI systems actively integrated into the design cycle.

elements_zh.where: 企业内部研发体系
elements_zh.what: 模型预训练加速与AI自进化研发
elements_zh.why: 算力供给与模型研发自动化升级

elements_en.what: Pretraining acceleration and AI-driven model design
elements_en.why: Compute scaling and automation of development pipelines

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 模型迭代已从算力堆叠转向“AI自我迭代”的正反馈循环，这意味着研发效率曲线将不再是线性的。这种技术范式的转移将大幅压缩竞争对手的窗口期，使基础设施能力与代码生成能力成为决定AGI终局的核心壁垒。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Model iteration is transitioning from compute-heavy brute force to an AI-driven feedback loop, signaling non-linear R&D efficiency gains. This paradigm shift compresses competitive windows, positioning infrastructure and code-generation capabilities as the primary moats for AGI.

title: "I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models
title_en:
"I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards.

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors).

That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it."

"I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards.

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors).

Apple recently posted a new job listing looking for an engineer to help lead this effort for Apple's

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman doesn't expect it to launch until at least the end of next year.
